## Purpose and Entry Points
Data Formulator is a local-first AI-assisted data exploration system: users load/connect data, conduct branching analyses in a Data Thread, generate/refine charts, and compose reports. Python serves the API and packaged frontend; React/Vite provides the browser UI. Main runtime entry points are `py-src/data_formulator/__main__.py`, `py-src/data_formulator/app.py`, and `src/index.tsx`. Desktop packaging adds `py-src/data_formulator/desktop.py` and `packaging/data_formulator_desktop.py`.

## Client Workspace and Interaction Model
The React application owns interactive workspace state, persisted sessions, API calls, auth token handling, and chart/table caches. `src/app/App.tsx` establishes the application shell; `src/app/store.ts` and `src/app/dfSlice.tsx` manage client data-thread/workspace state; `src/app/workspaceService.ts` bridges session persistence. The primary analyst experience is rendered through `src/views/DataFormulator.tsx`, `src/views/DataThread.tsx`, and `src/views/DataLoadingChat.tsx`.

## HTTP API, Sessions, and Contracts
The Python application exposes routes separating agent execution, tables/loading, session lifecycle, credentials, models, knowledge, and logs. Route modules are the boundary between frontend request contracts and backend services: `py-src/data_formulator/routes/agents.py`, `py-src/data_formulator/routes/tables.py`, and `py-src/data_formulator/routes/sessions.py`. Structured error handling is centralized in `py-src/data_formulator/error_handler.py` and `py-src/data_formulator/errors.py`, rather than leaking connector or agent failures directly to clients.

## Data Ingestion and Connector Boundary
A common connector/data-loader layer abstracts local files, folders, samples, databases, warehouses, cloud storage, and Superset. Core integration points are `py-src/data_formulator/data_connector.py`, `py-src/data_formulator/data_loader/external_data_loader.py`, and `py-src/data_formulator/data_loader/probe_utils.py`. Concrete loaders include PostgreSQL, BigQuery, Databricks, Kusto, S3, Azure Blob, MongoDB, and Superset. The UI discovers/configures these sources through `src/views/DataSourceSidebar.tsx` and `src/components/ConnectorFormCard.tsx`.

## Workspace, Catalog, and Data Execution
Loaded source data is organized in managed workspaces with metadata/catalog caching and Parquet-oriented utilities. `py-src/data_formulator/datalake/workspace.py`, `py-src/data_formulator/datalake/workspace_manager.py`, and `py-src/data_formulator/datalake/catalog_refresh.py` define this storage boundary; it can use ephemeral local workspaces or Azure Blob-backed workspaces. Declarative data operations are modeled, persisted, and executed by `py-src/data_formulator/data_operations/models.py`, `py-src/data_formulator/data_operations/repository.py`, and `py-src/data_formulator/data_operations/executor.py`.

## Agent and Analysis Pipeline
Agent requests receive workspace/context and use specialized capabilities for data loading, diagnostics, chart restyling, sorting, code explanation, and workflow distillation. Primary orchestration artifacts are `py-src/data_formulator/analyst/agent.py`, `py-src/data_formulator/agents/context.py`, and `py-src/data_formulator/agents/reasoning_log.py`; skill packages expose tool-oriented behavior in `py-src/data_formulator/analyst/skills/`. Model selection/configuration is separated in `py-src/data_formulator/model_registry.py` and `py-src/data_formulator/agent_config.py`. Supported external model providers include OpenAI, Azure, Ollama, and Anthropic through LiteLLM.

## Visualization, Reports, and Safety Boundaries
Chart semantics and Flint/Vega-Lite plot generation are backend workflow concerns in `py-src/data_formulator/workflows/chart_semantics.py` and `py-src/data_formulator/workflows/create_vl_plots.py`; interactive rendering and editing occur in `src/views/VisualizationView.tsx` and `src/views/ChartRenderService.tsx`. Reports are assembled in `src/views/ReportView.tsx`. Generated/executed work is constrained by sandbox implementations in `py-src/data_formulator/sandbox/` and security controls for paths, URL allowlisting, sanitization, code signing, and log redaction in `py-src/data_formulator/security/`.

## Deployment and Identity
The system runs via Python package, Docker, or desktop distribution; deployment definitions are `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, and `pyproject.toml`. Authentication supports OIDC, GitHub OAuth, Azure Easy Auth, Azure CLI, and Kusto OAuth, with token storage and local credential vault abstractions under `py-src/data_formulator/auth/`. The frontend auth lifecycle is represented by `src/app/AuthButton.tsx` and `src/app/OidcCallback.tsx`.
